prompt: Compute all real nonzero values of $b$ such that $bx^2-bx-b=0$ has $b$ as a solution.
Leo is at the bottom left corner of the grid. If he can only walk up and to the right, how many different paths can he take to the upper right corner?

solutions.title: Count paths to each intersection
solutions.body:
At every intersection of the drawn segments write the number of up/right paths from the lower-left corner; it is the sum of the numbers at the intersections immediately to its left and immediately below (along drawn segments). Every intersection on the left edge has exactly $1$ path. Along the bottom edge the numbers are $1,1$. On the long horizontal segment above the bottom cells the numbers are $1,2,\dots$, and the right edge from bottom to top reads $1,3,4,10,20$: for instance the right-edge node on that long segment gets $2+1=3$. Along the top edge, from left to right, the numbers are $1,4,10,20$. The upper-right corner receives $10$ from the node on the top edge just to its left and $10$ from the right-edge node just below it, so there are $10+10=20$ paths.

**Answer: 20**

prompt: The lines $y=2x+1$, $y=-\frac12x+6$, and $y=-2x-3$ split the plane into multiple regions. One of the regions has finite area. Compute the area of that region.

solutions.title: Triangle from the three lines
solutions.body:
The finite region is the triangle formed by the lines. Vertices: $y=2x+1$ and $y=-\frac12x+6$ meet at $A=(2,5)$; $y=2x+1$ and $y=-2x-3$ meet at $B=(-1,-1)$; $y=-\frac12x+6$ and $y=-2x-3$ meet at $C=(-6,9)$. The first two lines have slopes $2$ and $-\frac12$, whose product is $-1$, so they are perpendicular and the angle at $A$ is right. Then $AB=3\sqrt5$, $AC=4\sqrt5$ and the area is $\frac12\cdot3\sqrt5\cdot4\sqrt5=30$.

**Answer: 30**
